mechanism_narrative: The sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility (from -63.9 at t-2w to -32.6 at t-0w) restores weekday commuting and office-adjacent footfall, which mechanically lifts discretionary RETAIL_REC trips over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose 31.3 points from -63.9 at t-2w to -32.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: The forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the trailing 28-day mean while WORKPLACES continues to rise week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -50 percent change from baseline signals restored willingness to move through shared public space; transit-dependent retail catchments then recover, so RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -50 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -58.9 at t-2w to -44.4 at t-0w, crossing -50
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT exceeds -50, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean fails to exceed the preceding 28-day mean in more than half of observations.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS (-23.9 to -10.0) combined with falling RESIDENTIAL (16.7 to 11.6) shows discretionary time shifting out of the home into public space; that reallocation spills into nearby retail-and-recreation venues within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS above -15 and RESIDENTIAL below 12 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 13.9 points while RESIDENTIAL fell 5.1 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: When PARKS is above -15 and RESIDENTIAL below 12, RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Under an explicit de-confinement regime, the drawdown in RESIDENTIAL from 16.7 to 11.6 plus a rising TRANSIT series releases pent-up demand that converts into retail-and-recreation visits with a four-week policy-to-behavior lag.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL four-week mean below 15 while TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell in 3 of 4 weeks while TRANSIT rose 14.5 points from t-2w to t-0w
regime_hint: de-confinement easing under formal reopening orders
failure_condition: During declared easing regimes with RESIDENTIAL below 15 and TRANSIT rising, the forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has returned to -10.0 percent of baseline while RETAIL_REC remains at -33.3, leaving a 23.3-point suppressed-discretionary gap; that gap closes fastest in the first week after essential activity normalizes.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean at or above -12 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC (-33.3) trails GROCERY_PHARM (-10.0) by 23.3 points at t-0w
regime_hint: steady state with essential activity normalized
failure_condition: The RETAIL_REC minus GROCERY_PHARM gap widens rather than narrows over the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: Outdoor recreation is absorbing discretionary leisure spending: PARKS gained 13.9 points to -10.0 while RETAIL_REC gained only 4.8 points to -33.3, so seasonal outdoor substitution caps indoor retail-and-recreation and presses the forward four-week mean below the trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises above -12 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 3.9 points week-on-week to -10.0 while RETAIL_REC improved only 4.8 points over three weeks
failure_condition: The forward 28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the trailing mean while PARKS remains above -12.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery of TRANSIT (-44.4) and WORKPLACES (-32.6) in the same week marks a restored commute-and-errand round trip; the two series interact multiplicatively so retail-and-recreation footfall rises over the next two weeks only when both clear their thresholds.

evidence_refs: fact:at t-0w TRANSIT (-44.4) and WORKPLACES (-32.6) both posted their four-week best simultaneously
failure_condition: Weeks in which both TRANSIT exceeds -50 and WORKPLACES exceeds -40 are followed by a 28-day RETAIL_REC mean at or below the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: Policy-driven reduction of time at home is the binding constraint on retail: with RESIDENTIAL falling to 11.6 and GROCERY_PHARM stable near -10, each point of residential decline converts into out-of-home activity, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 12 while GROCERY_PHARM holds above -15
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from a 16.7 peak to 11.6 while GROCERY_PHARM recovered to -10.0
regime_hint: stay-at-home orders being lifted with essential capacity unchanged
